Package com.csse3200.game.components

Class TutorialComponent

java.lang.Object
com.csse3200.game.components.Component
com.csse3200.game.input.InputComponent
com.csse3200.game.components.TutorialComponent
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.badlogic.gdx.input.GestureDetector.GestureListener, com.badlogic.gdx.InputProcessor
public class TutorialComponent extends InputComponent
Observes raw keyboard and mouse input to advance a tutorial textbox through a configured sequence of steps. Each step lists the inputs that complete it: key names, mouse buttons pressed, and/or mouse buttons released. Any listed input completes the step unless requireAll is set, in which case every listed input must be seen. See configs/tut<n>.json for the sequences.

Input is never blocked, this component always returns false so the player input handler still receives every key and click. Priority exceeds the player handler so presses are seen before the player consumes them.

      public TutorialComponent(TextBoxComponent textBox, List<TutorialStepConfig> stepConfigs)
      Creates a tutorial over the given textbox.
      Parameters:
      textBox - tutorial textbox to advance, or null to ignore input
      stepConfigs - per-step trigger configs, one per textbox page; resolved to keycodes and mouse buttons eagerly
      Throws:

    • TutorialComponent

      public TutorialComponent(TextBoxComponent textBox, List<TutorialStepConfig> stepConfigs, Runnable onFinished, float autoDismissSeconds)
      Creates a tutorial with an optional deadline and completion callback.

      onFinished - run once the player completes the final step (not when the tutorial is dismissed early), or null for no callback
      autoDismissSeconds - seconds before the textbox dismisses itself without input; 0 or less waits forever for the player's steps
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a step names an unknown key or mouse button

    • tickAutoDismiss

      public void tickAutoDismiss(float delta)
      Advances the auto-dismiss deadline, if this tutorial has one. When it elapses the textbox closes like an early dismissal: the player's steps are no longer needed and onFinished does not run. This component is registered for input rather than entity updates, so the owning screen ticks it once per frame; calls are ignored once the tutorial is finished or dismissed.
      Parameters:
      delta - seconds since the previous frame

    • getCompletionKeycode

      public int getCompletionKeycode()
      The keycode that completed the most recent step, or 0 when no key has completed one (e.g. a mouse button did, or nothing has completed yet). Lets a choice tutorial such as tut0 report which option the player picked to its completion callback.
      Returns:
      the completing keycode
